title: Cost, efficiency, and outcomes of pulsed field ablation vs thermal ablation for atrial fibrillation
plainTitle: PFA or heat-based ablation: cost, time and results
summary: Compares newer pulsed-field ablation with traditional heat-based techniques, showing how technology choice affects procedure time, cost, and patient outcomes.

title: Atrial fibrillation and stroke prevention: 25 years of research at EP Europace journal
plainTitle: 25 years of preventing strokes in AF
summary: A quarter-century review of how stroke prevention in AF has evolved, from blood thinners to ablation and left atrial appendage closure.

title: Contemporary management of persistent atrial fibrillation
plainTitle: How persistent AF is treated today
summary: A practical guide to treating persistent AF today: when to ablate, which energy to use, and how to reduce the chance of the rhythm returning.

title: Use of Ablation Index-Guided Ablation Results in High Rates of Durable Pulmonary Vein Isolation
plainTitle: Measuring each burn so the result lasts
summary: Shows that measuring lesion quality during ablation leads to more durable vein isolation and fewer repeat procedures for paroxysmal AF.

title: Predictors of Device-Related Thrombus Following Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion
plainTitle: Who is at risk of clots on an LAAO device
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
summary: Identifies which patients are at higher risk of blood clots forming on LAAO devices, helping doctors time anticoagulation more safely.

title: How to use digital devices to detect and manage arrhythmias: an EHRA practical guide
plainTitle: Using smartwatches and phone apps to catch rhythm problems
summary: European expert guidance on using smartwatches and phone apps to spot irregular heart rhythms and decide when further testing is needed.

title: Silent cerebral lesions following catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: a state-of-the-art review
plainTitle: Brain safety after AF ablation
summary: Reviews the small brain changes sometimes seen on scans after AF ablation: what they mean, how common they are, and how to minimise risk.

title: Persistent and Recurrent Device-Related Thrombus After Left Atrial Appendage Closure
plainTitle: Clots on LAAO devices and who needs longer blood thinning
summary: Tracks how often clots form on or around LAAO devices over time, and which patients need longer blood-thinning after the procedure.

title: Outcomes of left atrial appendage occlusion vs. non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants
plainTitle: Closing the appendage versus newer blood thinners
summary: Real-world comparison of closing the appendage versus taking newer blood thinners, helping patients who cannot tolerate long-term anticoagulation.

title: Clinical outcomes with very high power very short duration ablation for atrial fibrillation
plainTitle: A faster, high-power ablation technique
summary: Tests a faster ablation technique that delivers high energy in brief bursts, with shorter procedure times and safety outcomes reported in detail.

title: Catheter ablation vs. thoracoscopic surgical ablation in long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation
plainTitle: Catheter ablation or keyhole surgery for long-standing AF
summary: Head-to-head comparison of keyhole surgical ablation versus catheter ablation for the hardest-to-treat persistent AF patients.

title: Catheter ablation as first-line treatment for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: a systematic review
plainTitle: Ablation as a first treatment, before years of tablets
summary: Synthesises the evidence for offering ablation early, before years of failed medications, in patients with intermittent AF.

title: Efficacy of Catheter Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation
plainTitle: Does ablation work for persistent AF?
summary: Landmark single-centre series showing that even persistent AF can be treated successfully with ablation when done by an experienced operator.

title: Ablation index, a novel marker of ablation lesion quality: prediction of pulmonary vein reconnection
plainTitle: A quality score that predicts whether veins stay isolated
summary: Introduces the Ablation Index, a measure of lesion quality that predicts whether veins stay isolated, reducing the need for repeat procedures.

title: Improvement in hard outcomes following catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: the debate is far from over
plainTitle: Does ablation prevent strokes and heart failure?
summary: Examines whether ablation genuinely reduces stroke and heart failure, not just symptom relief, and where the evidence still has gaps.

title: Impact of early ablation of atrial fibrillation on long-term outcomes
plainTitle: Why treating AF early pays off
summary: Follows patients over years to show that treating AF sooner, rather than waiting, is linked to better long-term heart health.

title: Quality of life and healthcare utilisation improvements after atrial fibrillation ablation
plainTitle: Quality of life after ablation
summary: Documents how successful ablation improves day-to-day wellbeing and reduces hospital visits, outcomes patients care about most.

title: Left Atrial Function Predicts Atrial Arrhythmia Recurrence Following Ablation of Long-Standing Persistent AF
plainTitle: Predicting who stays in rhythm after ablation
summary: Uses heart imaging to predict which persistent-AF patients are most likely to stay in normal rhythm after ablation.

title: Incidence and predictors of stroke and silent cerebral embolism following very high-power short-duration ablation
plainTitle: Stroke risk after fast high-power ablation
summary: Reports stroke and silent brain-embolism rates after fast high-power ablation, identifying patient factors that raise or lower risk.

title: Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation as First-Line Treatment for Typical Atrial Flutter
plainTitle: Freezing the veins to treat atrial flutter: the CRAFT trial
summary: Shows that freezing the pulmonary veins can treat atrial flutter as a first option, a less invasive alternative to conventional ablation.

title: Concurrent percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion and catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: state-of-the-art review
plainTitle: Ablation and LAAO in the same sitting
summary: Reviews when AF ablation and LAAO can be done in the same sitting, how the two procedures are sequenced, and what blood-thinning looks like afterwards.

title: Impact of pulsed-field ablation on the left atrial appendage diameter: insights from intra-procedural echocardiography
plainTitle: Does PFA change the size of the appendage?
summary: Measures the left atrial appendage before and after pulsed-field ablation, showing the pouch size does not change, which matters when ablation and LAAO are planned together.

title: Cardioneuroablation for vasovagal syncope and atrioventricular block: a step-by-step guide
plainTitle: Cardioneuroablation, step by step
summary: Practical guidance on cardioneuroablation for fainting and nerve-driven heart block: who it suits, how the procedure is done, and what to expect afterwards.

title: COnCOmitaNt pulsed field ablation-based pUlmonary vein isolation and lefT atrial appendage closure: the COCONUT study
plainTitle: PFA and LAAO in one procedure: the COCONUT study
summary: The largest study so far of pulsed-field ablation and appendage closure done in one sitting: 155 patients across 22 European centres, a 97% success rate, a 1.9% serious complication rate, and an average procedure time of 80 minutes.

title: Cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation as first-line treatment of typical atrial flutter: long-term outcomes of the CRAFT trial
plainTitle: Atrial flutter: three-year results of the CRAFT trial
summary: Follows the CRAFT trial patients to three years. Freezing the pulmonary veins controlled flutter as well as the standard ablation did, and led to less atrial fibrillation afterwards.

title: Impact of pulmonary vein isolation on atrial arrhythmias in patients with typical atrial flutter: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
plainTitle: Treating the veins too, when ablating flutter
summary: Pools seven randomised trials, 902 patients in all, and finds that isolating the pulmonary veins alongside or instead of the standard flutter ablation roughly halves later atrial arrhythmias, mostly by preventing new AF.

title: Cryoablation compared with radiofrequency ablation for atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia: analysis of factors contributing to acute and follow-up outcome
plainTitle: Freezing or heat for the commonest type of SVT
summary: Compares two ways of ablating AVNRT, the most common type of SVT. Freezing was gentler on the heart’s wiring but the rhythm came back more often, so heat remained the more reliable choice.

title: Current case mix and results of catheter ablation of regular supraventricular tachycardia: are we giving unrealistic expectations to patients?
plainTitle: Honest success rates for SVT ablation
summary: Looks at nearly 400 SVT ablations in one large centre and asks whether the success rates quoted to patients are realistic. Repeat procedures did less well than first ones, which is a reason to get it right first time.

title: A randomized-controlled trial comparing conventional with minimal catheter approaches for the mapping and ablation of regular supraventricular tachycardias
plainTitle: Fewer catheters, same result: a simpler ablation
summary: A randomised trial of 200 patients showing that SVT and atrial flutter can be mapped and ablated with fewer catheters, just as safely and effectively, and at lower cost.

title: Intranasal etripamil for rapid treatment of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia
plainTitle: A nasal spray to stop an SVT attack at home
summary: Reviews etripamil, a nasal spray being developed so that people can stop an episode of SVT themselves without an emergency visit, and where it might fit alongside ablation.

title: Frequent premature atrial contractions as a signalling marker of atrial cardiomyopathy, incident atrial fibrillation, and stroke
plainTitle: When extra beats are a warning sign
summary: Explains why frequent extra beats from the upper chambers, once thought harmless, are now linked to a higher chance of developing AF and stroke, and what that means for monitoring and treatment.

title: Smart wearables for cardiac monitoring: real-world use beyond atrial fibrillation
plainTitle: What smartwatches can and cannot tell you
summary: Reviews how wearables, patches and phone apps are used to monitor heart rhythm beyond AF, and what a reading from one can and cannot tell a doctor.

title: Cardioneuroablation for the treatment of reflex syncope and functional bradyarrhythmias: a scientific statement of EHRA, HRS, APHRS and LAHRS
plainTitle: International guidance on cardioneuroablation
summary: The joint European, American, Asia-Pacific and Latin American position on cardioneuroablation as an alternative to a pacemaker for reflex fainting and nerve-driven slow rhythms: who it suits and how it should be done.

title: The "heart brain" and neuromodulation for vasovagal syncope
plainTitle: The heart’s own nerves, and how to calm them
summary: Explains the network of nerves on the surface of the heart that can trigger a faint, and how catheter treatment of those nerves has moved from experiment to everyday practice in major hospitals.

title: Cardioneuroablation for treatment of atrioventricular block
plainTitle: Treating heart block without a pacemaker
summary: Reports patients whose heart block was driven by an overactive nerve supply and treated with cardioneuroablation rather than a pacemaker, with encouraging results in carefully selected people.

title: Outcomes of atrioventricular node ablation and pacing in patients with heart failure and atrial fibrillation: from cardiac resynchronization therapy to His bundle pacing
plainTitle: Pace and ablate: when a pacemaker is the answer for AF
journal: Journal of Cardiovascular Development and Disease
summary: Reviews the pace and ablate approach for people with AF and heart failure, where a pacemaker takes over the rhythm, and compares the pacing options from resynchronisation to His bundle pacing.

title: Predictors of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy in patients undergoing AV nodal ablation: insights from a Delphi process and retrospective cohort study
plainTitle: Choosing the right pacemaker before an AV node ablation
summary: Liverpool data on 323 patients showing which people are most likely to develop a weakened heart from standard pacing after AV node ablation, so that they can be offered a more physiological pacing system up front.

title: Outcome of left atrial appendage occlusion in high-risk patients
plainTitle: LAAO for people who cannot take blood thinners
summary: Liverpool’s first 83 LAAO patients, nearly all with previous major bleeding. The device was implanted successfully in 99%, with the complications and one-year stroke and bleeding rates reported openly.

title: Long-term outcomes of left atrial appendage occlusion in high-risk atrial fibrillation patients: 4-year follow up data
plainTitle: Four years after LAAO
summary: Follows 71 high-risk patients for around four years after an Amulet implant. The stroke rate stayed low, though these frail patients remained at risk from other illnesses and from bleeding.

title: Left atrial appendage occlusion: British Cardiovascular Intervention Society and British Heart Rhythm Society position statement
plainTitle: The UK standard for LAAO
summary: The British position statement setting out who should be offered LAAO, how the procedure should be planned and performed, and the minimum experience an implanting centre and doctor should have.

title: Left atrial appendage occlusion: a choice or a last resort? How to approach the patient
plainTitle: LAAO: a last resort, or a choice?
summary: Weighs whether appendage closure should be reserved for people who cannot take blood thinners or offered as a genuine alternative, and sets out how to approach the decision with each patient.
